body.statement: For every rational \(c\in\mathcal C_K\cap\mathbb Q^K\) and every rational \(\eta>0\), \(\mathsf{Cert}(c,\eta)\) terminates with a finite symbolic record \(\Gamma\). The record contains \(N\), finite rational and real-algebraic data, proof-checkable monotone bounds, and an explicitly specified total evaluator \(\mathsf{Eval}_{\Gamma}\). For every requested integer \(n\ge N\), \[\mathsf{Eval}_{\Gamma}(n)=(B_n,U_n)\in\mathbb A_{\mathrm R}^2,\qquad B_n\le R_n(c)\le U_n,\qquad n^{4/3}(U_n-B_n)\le\eta.\] Each \(B_n\) is the exact Bayes risk of a finite-schedule prior valid against all outcome-independent designs, and each \(U_n\) is the exact worst-schedule risk of a rationalized total full-label rule under the independent allocation \(q^\star\). Real-algebraic values are represented by square-free integer polynomials, rational isolating intervals, and Thom-sign data, and every arithmetic or order operation is certified by exact rational algorithms. As a continuity corollary, every real \(c\in\mathcal C_K\) admits normalization-preserving rational brackets \(c'\) with the same active support and signs such that \[|\sqrt{R_n(c)}-\sqrt{R_n(c')}|\le\omega(c,c').\] Choosing bracket errors \(o(n^{-5/6})\) transfers the coefficient and risk expansion mathematically to \(c\), without asserting a Turing evaluator for an unrepresented real contrast.
body.justification: An all-future exact certificate distinguishes a theorem-backed second-order recommendation from numerical convergence at selected sample sizes.
body.gap: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) and Hull (2026) give finite reductions, while Aronow and Lopatto (2026), Theorem 3, gives exact witnesses only under unbiasedness; none supplies this uniform multi-arm asymptotic certificate.
body.consumer: Trial planners can certify at a given horizon whether the proposed independent allocation is within a chosen normalized risk tolerance of the unrestricted optimum, while rational enclosures support mathematical verification of prespecified real-valued weights.
body.proof_tex:
Fix rational \(c\in\mathcal C_K\) and rational \(\eta>0\).  We describe a finite search, prove that it terminates, and identify the exact witnesses it returns.

First, the gauge lemma enumerates rational primal and dual basic feasible solutions and returns exact rational \(\kappa(c)>0\), \(\ell^\star\), and \(g^\star\).  The explicit basis used in the all-count proof, nonnegative response representations of its columns, and the constants \(L_v,L_j,k_j,F_j,L,\Gamma\) are obtained by rational arithmetic and maxima over finite response alphabets.  Thus all non-Airy constants in (10)--(35) of that proof are exact rational data.

Second, the one-dimensional Airy data are effective.  One concrete enclosure procedure uses the power-series recurrence obtained from \(A''(x)=xA(x)\), rational interval quadrature for the two initial constants, and interval Taylor remainders on successive compact intervals.  Interval sign certificates and the differential equation isolate the rightmost negative zero of \(A'\); it is simple because at such a zero the equation gives \(A''=xA\ne0\).  Bisection therefore converges to it.  The same interval recurrence, followed by the explicit scaling by rational \(\kappa(c)\), gives arbitrarily narrow rational enclosures of \(C_A\), \(\Lambda_c\), \(h_\kappa\), \(h_\kappa'\), and valid tail and Lipschitz majorants.  Each requested enclosure is certified by finitely many rational inequalities, and refinement terminates by convergence of the series and the isolating bisection.

Choose a rational error budget \(\epsilon_0<\eta/32\).  Enumerate compact rational piecewise-polynomial functions until exact integration and the Airy interval enclosure certify
\[
4\frac{\int f'^2}{\int f^2}
+\kappa(c)\frac{\int|x|f^2}{\int f^2}
\le\Lambda_c+\epsilon_0.
\tag{36}
\]
The approximation argument in the all-count proof proves that this enumeration terminates.  Choose rational \(\varepsilon>0\) with \(\varepsilon\sum_jk_j\le\epsilon_0\).  Every tube probability is piecewise polynomial in \((x,h)\) with coefficients in \(\mathbb Q(n^{-1/3})\).  Exact integration over its finitely many sign cells therefore gives every schedule mass in the ordered real-algebraic field.

For the upper rule, interval evaluation of \(h_\kappa\) on each algebraic score is refined until a rational number within \(n^{-2}\) is selected, after which projection is performed exactly.  Denote this finite rational table by \(\widetilde\delta_n\).  Because the target and both reported values lie in \([-1,1]\), pointwise rounding changes squared loss by at most \(4n^{-2}\).  The upper proof and its explicit Taylor bounds consequently provide a proof-checkable inequality of the form
\[
\max_y\mathcal R_n(\mathcal D_n^\star,\widetilde\delta_n;y)
\le n^{-1}-(\Lambda_c-4\epsilon_0)n^{-4/3}
\tag{37}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Likewise, (25)--(35), (36), and the choice of \(\varepsilon\) provide
\[
\inf_r\operatorname{BR}_{\Pi_n}(r)
\ge n^{-1}-(\Lambda_c+4\epsilon_0)n^{-4/3}
\tag{38}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Every sufficient condition used for (37)--(38) is a monotone inequality between explicit rational constants and negative rational powers of \(n\).  Sequential search therefore finds a finite \(N\) after which they all hold.  Enlarging \(N\) absorbs the \(4n^{-2}\) rounding term and ensures \(8\epsilon_0\le\eta\).

It remains to specify the exact endpoints, rather than merely their analytic bounds.  Let \(\nu_n(y)\) be the exact algebraic mass of schedule \(y\) under the tube prior.  For a fixed assignment \(z\), let \(O_z(y)\) be its observed string and set
\[
D_{z,o}=\sum_{y:O_z(y)=o}\nu_n(y).
\]
Its exact posterior Bayes risk is
\[
\operatorname{BR}_{\nu_n}(z)
=\sum_y\nu_n(y)\tau_c(y)^2
-\sum_{o:D_{z,o}>0}
\frac{\left\{\sum_{y:O_z(y)=o}\nu_n(y)\tau_c(y)\right\}^2}{D_{z,o}}.
\tag{39}
\]
Define
\[
B_n=\min_{z\in\mathcal A_K^n}\operatorname{BR}_{\nu_n}(z).
\tag{40}
\]
This is the Bayes value against all outcome-independent designs: after observing \(z\), the posterior mean is optimal, and a mixture over assignments averages the conditional risks, whose minimum is (40).  Hence minimax is at least \(B_n\).  Define the exact upper endpoint
\[
U_n=\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times K}}
\sum_{z\in\mathcal A_K^n}\left(\prod_iq_{z_i}^\star\right)
\{\widetilde\delta_n(z,O_z(y))-\tau_c(y)\}^2.
\tag{41}
\]
This is the worst-schedule risk of one admissible design-estimator pair, so \(R_n(c)\le U_n\).  All sets in (39)--(41) are finite.  Field operations and comparisons on their algebraic entries terminate using resultants, isolating intervals, Thom signs, and Sturm sequences.  Thus \(B_n,U_n\in\mathbb A_{\mathrm R}\) are exact, and (37)--(38) imply for every \(n\ge N\)
\[
B_n\le R_n(c)\le U_n,
\qquad n^{4/3}(U_n-B_n)\le8\epsilon_0\le\eta.
\]
The finite constants, interval certificates, monotone tail inequalities, and the finite enumeration algorithms (39)--(41) constitute \(\Gamma\); they define a total evaluator for every integer \(n\ge N\).  This proves termination and every advertised exactness claim, without a complexity bound.

We finally justify the real-contrast transfer.  If \(c,c'\) lie in the same sign chamber and obey the two normalizations, then \(u=c-c'\) has zero sum.  For every binary vector \(t\),
\[
|u^\top t|\le\frac12\|u\|_1=\omega(c,c').
\tag{42}
\]
Minkowski's inequality applied to any fixed design-estimator pair, followed in both directions by the infimum and supremum operations, gives the exact modulus
\[
|\sqrt{R_n(c)}-\sqrt{R_n(c')}|\le\omega(c,c').
\tag{43}
\]
Normalization-preserving rational contrasts with the same support and signs are dense because the positive coordinates form the relative interior of a rational simplex of total mass one, and the absolute values of the negative coordinates form another.

The required local uniformity is also explicit.  In a fixed sign chamber the constraint matrix of the gauge program and its right side \(v\) are constant.  Its optimum is the minimum, over finitely many basic feasible solutions \(\lambda\), of
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t(c^\top t)^2.
\]
Hence \(\kappa(c)\), and therefore \(\Lambda_c\), is locally Lipschitz.  On a sufficiently small compact neighborhood of a fixed permitted \(c\), active \(|c_a|\) and \(\kappa(c)\) are bounded away from zero; the finitely many primal masses, the dual feasible boxes, \(B^{-1}\), the response representations, and all constants in the upper and lower remainder bounds are uniformly bounded.  The proofs above therefore give a remainder \(o(n^{-4/3})\) uniformly on that neighborhood.

Choose rational \(c^{(n)}\) in the same chamber with
\(e_n=\omega(c,c^{(n)})=o(n^{-5/6})\).  The exact certified endpoints for \(c^{(n)}\) obey, by (43),
\[
\left[\max\{0,\sqrt{B_n}-e_n\}\right]^2
\le R_n(c)\le
\left[\sqrt{U_n}+e_n\right]^2.
\tag{44}
\]
Uniformly, \(B_n,U_n=O(n^{-1})\), so the additional width in (44) is
\(O(e_nn^{-1/2}+e_n^2)=o(n^{-4/3})\).  Local uniformity and \(\Lambda_{c^{(n)}}\to\Lambda_c\) transfer the coefficient and expansion to the real contrast.  The construction only asserts existence of the rational brackets for an arbitrary represented real and does not assert a Turing evaluator for an unrepresented real number.
